issues.legal_issue: A suit to determine the boundary between neighbouring properties is maintainable when the owners dispute its location and the requested cooperation in fixing it is not given.
material_facts: The plaintiff and the defendant owned neighbouring properties and disputed the precise boundary between them.
The parties agreed on a method for ascertaining the boundary and nominated arbitrators, but the arbitrators declined to demarcate it.
The plaintiff sought a court decree identifying and demarcating the property boundary.
issues.conclusion: The boundary-demarcation suit was maintainable, and the appeal challenging that conclusion was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure, civil courts may try suits of a civil nature unless their jurisdiction is expressly or impliedly barred. A dispute between neighbouring owners about the location of their boundary is civil in nature, and no equitable circumstance need be established as a prerequisite to suit. The Court declined to import the English distinction between legal and equitable estates reflected in Wake v. Conyers and followed in Kavasji Jamsetji v. Hormasji Nassaravanjishet, and held that Rayappan v. Yagappan Nadar did not state the correct law and must be overruled.

rule.if: boundary_demarcation_suit and neighbouring_owners_dispute and boundary_location_disputed and cooperation_demanded_but_not_given and not jurisdictional_bar

predicates.boundary_demarcation_suit: A party brought a suit seeking judicial determination or demarcation of a property boundary.
predicates.neighbouring_owners_dispute: Owners of neighbouring properties disputed the boundary separating their properties.
predicates.boundary_location_disputed: The precise location of the boundary was uncertain or contested.
predicates.cooperation_demanded_but_not_given: A party sought the other party's cooperation in fixing the boundary, but that cooperation was not given.
predicates.jurisdictional_bar: A law expressly or impliedly bars the civil court from trying the suit.

issues.definition: When neighbouring property owners dispute an uncertain boundary, a party has sought cooperation to fix it without success, and no jurisdictional bar applies, the boundary-demarcation suit is maintainable.
